les: Twee mense wat die demokrasie help bou het
kaps_punt: Gevallestudie: Fatima Meer: 'n leier in die bou van demokrasie; Gevallestudie: Pius Langa: Hoofregter van die Grondwetlike Hof: 2005 - 2009

items.bewering: Fatima Meer was 'n aktivis, 'n skrywer en 'n dosent in sosiologie.
items.bron: SAHO, sahistory.org.za/people/fatima-meer: 'Political leader, academic, publisher, author, human rights and gender activist'; began lecturing Sociology at the University of Natal in 1956; 'produced over forty books'.

items.bewering: Sy het die Durban and District Women's League help stig.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fatima Meer' (citing the SAHO timeline): 'She helped to establish the Durban and District Women's League on 4 October 1952 as a group of 70 women.' The SAHO biography ties the league to the aftermath of the 1949 Durban riots. The lesson gives no founding year, so the dating difference does not touch it.

items.bewering: Bertha Mkhize was die voorsitter en Meer die sekretaris.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Fatima Meer' (citing the SAHO timeline): 'Bertha Mkhize became the chairperson and Meer became the secretary of the league.' The SAHO biography agrees.

items.bewering: Die land het mense volgens bevolkingsgroep verdeel.
items.bron: SAHO dated event 'Parliament passes legislation separating people of South Africa into four distinct races': the Population Registration Act No. 30 of 1950 classified people into White, Black, Coloured and Indian; the SAHA material on race classification describes what the classification decided.

items.bewering: In die liga het Indiese vroue en Afrikavroue saam gewerk.
items.bron: SAHO, sahistory.org.za/node/16709: the league brought Indian and African women together and is described as the first South African organisation with a common Indian and African membership.

items.bewering: Meer was self een van die Indiese vroue.
items.bron: SAHO biography, sahistory.org.za/people/fatima-meer, and Wikipedia 'Fatima Meer': she was a South African of Indian descent, and her 1999 group campaigned among Indian voters.

items.bewering: In 1956 was sy die eerste nie-wit vrou wat aangestel is om aan 'n wit Suid-Afrikaanse universiteit klas te gee.
items.bron: SAHO biography: 'the first Black woman to be appointed as a lecturer at a white South African University', lecturing at the University of Natal from 1956. Carleton University's account of Shireen Hassim's biography of Meer: the first non-white woman appointed at a 'white' university. Britannica, quoted by Wikipedia, words it more broadly as the first non-white person in that position, which does not contradict the lesson's narrower claim. No university record was reached, so the claim rests on biographical accounts, including her biographer's.

items.bewering: Sy het toe van buite die regering aan 'n vryer land gewerk. Haar stryd het lank voor daardie jaar begin.
items.bron: SAHO biography and timeline: her organising predates 1956 (the league after the 1949 riots or in 1952, and her first banning order in 1952 or 1954). She held no government office.

items.bewering: In 1954 is sy die eerste keer verban. Ander bronne gee 1952 as die jaar van dieselfde bevel.
items.bron: Sources disagree, and the weight of them falls the other way from the lesson. The SAHO biography gives 1952, three years, under the Suppression of Communism Act. Wikipedia, citing Britannica, says she was 'first "banned" in 1952 for three years'. The SAHO timeline lists a 1952 order for five years, flagged 'Check this date', AND a separate 1954 order for two years covering gatherings, publishing, public speaking and leaving Durban. Dasarath Chetty's pictorial tribute on SAHO gives 1954, for five years. So 1952 has more sources than 1954, and one source (the SAHO timeline) shows two separate orders, which goes against the lesson's 'dieselfde bevel'. A person should decide: either lead with 1952 as the better-supported first ban and keep the one covering sentence about 1954, or drop the year and say she was banned in the early 1950s. Either way, 'the same order' is not established and should not be asserted. If the conflict sentence is kept, this item is the candidate for a named acceptance.

items.bewering: Die bevel het haar tot die Durban-distrik beperk en haar alle openbare byeenkomste verbied. Dit het ook verbied dat haar skryfwerk gedruk word.
items.bron: SAHO biography on the 1952 order: confined to Durban; 'The banning order prohibited her from attending all public gatherings and from having her work published.' The SAHO timeline gives the same terms for its 1954 entry. The terms are confirmed whichever year the order dates from; the year itself is the open item above.

items.bewering: In 1976 is sy van Augustus tot Desember sonder verhoor aangehou, deels in alleenopsluiting.
items.bron: SAHO timeline 1928-2010: 'Detained without trial from August to December 1976 part of it in solitary confinement.' The SAHO biography agrees: detained late August, held at Fort Prison, released in December, with parts of the detention in solitary confinement.

items.bewering: Die bevel en die sel het haar nie laat ophou werk nie.
items.bron: SAHO biography: she stayed on the University of Natal staff until 1988 and was 'the only banned person who was ever granted permission to teach'; she was charged twice for breaking her orders and went on publishing and organising.

items.bewering: Pius Langa het in die Departement van Justisie as tolk en boodskapper gewerk.
items.blok: Pius Langa se pad deur die howe
items.bron: SAHO, sahistory.org.za/people/pius-nkonzo-langa: 'messenger of court and interpreter for the Department of Justice'.

items.bewering: Van daar het hy stap vir stap landdros geword.
items.blok: Pius Langa se pad deur die howe
items.bron: SAHO Langa biography: 'Through sheer hard work Langa rose to become a prosecutor and later a magistrate.'

items.bewering: Naas sy werk het hy sy regsgrade deur afstandsonderrig behaal.
items.blok: Pius Langa se pad deur die howe
items.bron: SAHO Langa biography: law studies by correspondence through UNISA, a B Iuris in 1973 and an LLB about 1976, while he was a civil servant. Wikipedia 'Pius Langa' agrees.

items.bewering: In 1977 het hy uit die staat se diens bedank en advokaat geword.
items.blok: Pius Langa se pad deur die howe
items.bron: SAHO Langa biography: he resigned from the department in 1977, and in June 1977 he was 'admitted as an Advocate of the Supreme Court in Natal'. The Constitutional Court collection (collections.concourt.org.za) records his 1977 admission as an advocate.

items.bewering: Daarna het hy jare lank aktiviste in die hof verdedig.
items.blok: Pius Langa se pad deur die howe
items.bron: SAHO Langa biography: he represented anti-apartheid activists in Natal, the Eastern Cape and Cape Town. Wikipedia: he specialised in defending anti-apartheid activists accused of political offences.

items.bewering: President Nelson Mandela het Langa in 1994 as een van die Konstitusionele Hof se eerste elf regters benoem.
items.bron: Constitutional Court, concourt.org.za, 'The appointment of the judges', and SAHO 'Appointment of judges': under the interim constitution Mandela appointed a President (Chaskalson), four judges from the Supreme Court, and six from the JSC shortlist, Langa among them. That is eleven in all, and the eleven first sat on 15 February 1995. SAHO dates Langa's appointment to October 1994.

items.bewering: Van 2005 tot 2009 was hy die Hoofregter van Suid-Afrika.
items.bron: SAHO Langa biography and Wikipedia 'Pius Langa': Chief Justice from 1 June 2005 until he retired in October 2009.

items.bewering: President Thabo Mbeki het hom die amp gegee.
items.bron: Mail & Guardian, 11 March 2005, 'Mbeki taps Langa': Mbeki nominated the Deputy Chief Justice to succeed Chaskalson, and the appointment is made under section 174(3) of the Constitution.

items.bewering: Die Hoofregter is sedert 2001 die hoof van die Konstitusionele Hof.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Sixth Amendment of the Constitution of South Africa' and 'Arthur Chaskalson': the 2001 amendment renamed the President of the Constitutional Court as Chief Justice, in force from 21 November 2001. Chaskalson was Chief Justice from November 2001.

items.bewering: Albei het gewerk aan 'n demokrasie wat nog nie bestaan het nie. Meer het dit as aktivis en skrywer gedoen, en Langa van 1977 af as advokaat.
items.bron: SAHO biographies of Meer and Langa, as for the items above: Meer's activism and writing from the 1940s-50s onward, and Langa's defence of activists from his 1977 admission.

items.bewering: Ná 1994 het albei oor die nuwe demokrasie gaan waak. Langa het dit tot 2009 van binne die howe gedoen.
items.bron: SAHO Langa biography: Constitutional Court judge from 1994, Chief Justice until his 2009 retirement.

items.bewering: Van 1999 af het Meer 'n groep burgers in Chatsworth gelei. Hulle het in die hof teen die nuwe staat se eie onwettige uitsettings gewen.
items.bron: SAHO timeline: in May 1999 she was one of the founders of the Concerned Citizens' Group, which 'brought and won two successful interdicts against the Council against unlawful evictions' in Chatsworth. SAHO biography: 'She organised successful interdicts against unlawful eviction, and won reprieves with costs.' Libcom's 'Anti-eviction actions in Chatsworth' (after Desai, We Are the Poors) confirms the Chatsworth eviction struggle. The 'state' here is the Durban municipal council, which is local government and therefore part of the post-1994 state.

items.bewering: demokrasie: 'n Manier van regeer waar die mense self kies wie regeer.
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'democracy': 'a form of government in which people choose leaders by voting'.

items.bewering: aktivis: Iemand wat veldtog voer en mense saamkry om iets in 'n land te verander.
items.bron: Learner's Dictionary (learnersdictionary.com) 'activist': a person who uses or supports strong actions such as public protests to help make changes in politics or society. Vocabulary.com agrees.

items.bewering: universiteit: 'n Plek waar mense ná hulle skooljare studeer en 'n graad kan kry.
items.bron: UNISA Open Distance e-Learning policy (unisa.ac.za): a university is a higher-education institution teaching post-school students for degrees. This is a plain-meaning definition with no factual risk.

items.bewering: verbanning: 'n Bevel van die apartheidsregering wat 'n mens se vryheid vir 'n tyd ingekort het. So 'n bevel kon iemand tot een plek beperk, openbare byeenkomste vir hom verbied of keer dat sy woorde gedruk word. Nie elke bevel het dieselfde gesê nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Suppression of Communism Act, 1950' and the UCT South African Banned Persons project (ibali.uct.ac.za): the minister could restrict movement and expression, confine people to an area, and bar them from gatherings, and the terms varied by order. Publication bans are confirmed by Meer's own order (SAHO). Orders ran for fixed periods. Out of remit, noted for the language step only: Afrikaans also used 'inperking' for these orders, and 'verbanning' can mean exile.

items.bewering: alleenopsluiting: Wanneer 'n mens alleen in 'n sel aangehou word, weg van ander mense.
items.bron: UN Nelson Mandela Rules, Rule 44, as quoted by John Howard Society and ICRC: confinement without meaningful human contact. The lesson's definition is a fair simplification.

items.bewering: tolk: Iemand wat mondeling uit een taal in 'n ander taal vertaal.
items.bron: AIIC, 'Interpreter or Translator?' (aiic.org): interpreters carry meaning across languages in spoken form, and translators work on written text.

items.bewering: landdros: Iemand wat in 'n laer hof oor sake beslis.
items.bron: Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, s166 (justice.gov.za): Magistrates' Courts sit below the High Court. A landdros presides over a magistrate's court.

items.bewering: advokaat: Iemand wat wette bestudeer het en wat sake in die hof bepleit; 'n prokureur vra hom gewoonlik om dit te doen.
items.bron: Legal Practice Act s34(2)(a), as summarised by Mondaq/ENS on referral advocates, and Rösemann v General Council of the Bar (SCA 2003, saflii.org): referral advocates take briefs from attorneys and argue in court. Trust-account advocates may take instructions directly, which 'gewoonlik' allows for.

items.bewering: afstandsonderrig: Studie waar 'n mens nie klas by die skool of die universiteit bywoon nie. Studiestof en opdragte kom in die plek van die klas, en die student werk self daardeur.
items.bron: UNISA Open Distance e-Learning policy: teaching methods for students who are geographically apart from the institution and their tutors.

items.bewering: regbank: Al die howe en regters van 'n land saam.
items.bron: Superior Courts Act 10 of 2013 (Afrikaans text, parliament.gov.za) uses 'regbank' for the judiciary. Constitution s165-166: judicial authority is vested in the courts.

items.bewering: Hoofregter: Die regter wat vandag aan die hoof van die land se hele regbank staan.
items.bron: Constitution s165(6): 'The Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary'. The Superior Courts Act 2013 (Afrikaans) says 'die Hoofregter die hoof van die regbank is'. The word 'vandag' correctly marks this as the present arrangement.

items.bewering: Konstitusionele Hof: Die hof met die laaste sê oor die Grondwet, en vandag ook die hoogste hof in Suid-Afrika in alle sake; 'n beslissing van 'n ander hoër hof, soos die Hooggeregshof, dat 'n wet van die Parlement die Grondwet oortree, geld eers wanneer hierdie hof dit bevestig.
items.bron: Constitution s167(3)(a): 'is the highest court of the Republic'; s167(3)(b)(ii): it may decide any other matter on leave, where the matter raises an arguable point of law of general public importance; s167(5) and s172(2)(a): an order of constitutional invalidity by the SCA or the High Court 'has no force unless it is confirmed by the Constitutional Court'. The phrase 'in alle sake' is a fair Grade 6 rendering of 'highest court of the Republic', although strictly a non-constitutional matter reaches the court only with its leave.

items.bewering: Hooggeregshof: Een van die hoër howe; hy staan hoër as 'n landdroshof.
items.bron: Constitution s166: the High Court of South Africa is listed above the Magistrates' Courts, and s170 limits courts of lower status than the High Court.

opsomming: One item needs a person: the lesson says Meer was first banned in 1954 and that other sources give 1952 for the same order, but most sources reached (SAHO biography, Britannica via Wikipedia, the SAHO timeline) give 1952, and the SAHO timeline lists 1952 and 1954 as two separate orders, so both the lead year and 'the same order' are unsettled. Everything else, including the 1956 'first' and the 'first eleven judges', is confirmed. The lesson has no analogies.
